title: My day
goal: Describe what you do during the day with everyday -er verbs and time phrases like le matin and à 8 heures.

items.fr: je travaille, nous travaillons, ils travaillent
items.en: regular -er verbs: all six present-tense forms

drills.en: What time do you get home?
They listen to the radio in the evening.
drills.explain: ils → -ent, and the -ent is silent: ils écoutent.

drills.en: Do you work in the morning?

drills.explain: French has one present tense: je regarde = I watch / I'm watching.

items.en: spelling change in the nous form of manger and commencer

drills.explain: Before -ons, c becomes ç to keep the soft s sound: commençons.
Before -ons, g needs an e to keep the soft j sound: mangeons.
Verbs in -cer take ç before o: nous commençons.

example.fr: Le soir, on regarde la télé.
example.en: In the evening, we watch TV.

items.note: No word for “at”: regarder la télé.
No word for “to”: écouter la radio.

items.en: to finish, to end (work, a class)
to go home, to get home

blocks.title: Neighbours chatting in Gatineau
blocks.context: Sofia meets her neighbour Karim outside their building.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.en: Karim, do you work in Ottawa?

lines.speaker: Karim
lines.fr: Oui. Je commence à 8 heures le matin et je termine à 16 heures.
lines.en: Yes. I start at 8 in the morning and I finish at 4 p.m.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Et tu rentres à quelle heure ?
lines.en: And what time do you get home?

lines.speaker: Karim
lines.fr: Je rentre à 17 heures. Le soir, je cuisine avec ma femme.
lines.en: I get home at 5. In the evening, I cook with my wife.

lines.speaker: Karim
lines.fr: Nous mangeons à 18 heures avec les enfants. Et à 20 heures, on regarde la télé.
lines.en: We eat at 6 with the children. And at 8, we watch TV.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Moi, je travaille l'après-midi. Je commence à 13 heures et je termine à 21 heures.
lines.en: Me, I work in the afternoon. I start at 1 p.m. and I finish at 9 p.m.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.fr: Je rentre, je mange et j'écoute la radio.
lines.en: I go home, I eat and I listen to the radio.

blocks.body: Listen first. Notice how many verbs end in **-e** and sound almost the same: [[travaille, commence, termine, rentre, cuisine]]. Then tap a line to check the English.

blocks.title: You already know the pattern
blocks.body:
In Unit 2 you learned [[parler]] and [[habiter]]. Good news: almost every verb ending in **-er** works exactly the same way. Take off **-er** and add the ending for each person.

French has **one** present tense. [[Je travaille]] means *I work* **and** *I'm working*. There is no extra word for *am* or *do*.

blocks.title: Travailler (to work) in the present
head: travailler
English
rows: you work (formal, or more than one person)
blocks.note: Four forms sound **exactly the same**: [[travaille, travailles, travaille, travaillent]]. The endings **-e, -es, -ent** are silent. Only [[-ons]] and [[-ez]] are heard.

blocks.title: Two verbs with a small spelling change
head: manger (to eat)
commencer (to start)
blocks.note: Only the **nous** form changes. A *g* or *c* before *o* would sound hard (like *go*, *cot*), so French writes [[mangeons]] (soft *j* sound) and [[commençons]] (soft *s* sound).

blocks.title: When? Time phrases
blocks.pattern: verbe + le matin / l'après-midi / le soir / à 8 heures
blocks.note: [[Le matin]], [[l'après-midi]] and [[le soir]] need **no preposition** and describe what you usually do. Use [[à]] + a clock time for an exact time. Time phrases can go at the start or the end of the sentence.

examples.en: In the afternoon, she prepares her classes.

examples.fr: Ils commencent à 8 heures et ils terminent à 17 heures.
examples.en: They start at 8 and finish at 5 p.m.

blocks.body:
Three sound rules make these verbs easy to say:

- **Silent endings:** [[je mange]], [[tu manges]], [[ils mangent]] all sound like *mahnj*.
- **Élision:** before a vowel, [[je]] becomes [[j']]: [[j'écoute]], [[j'habite]].
- **Liaison:** [[nous]], [[vous]], [[ils]] and [[elles]] link with a *z* sound before a vowel: [[nous‿écoutons]], [[ils‿écoutent]]. That *z* is often the only way to hear that *they* is plural.

examples.en: he listens — they listen (hear the z)

blocks.body:
- **No “am” for -ing:** [[Je suis travaille]] is wrong. Say [[Je travaille]] (I'm working).
- **No extra little words:** [[écouter la radio]] (listen **to**), [[regarder la télé]] (look **at**). Don't add [[à]].
- **No preposition with le matin:** say [[le matin]], not [[dans le matin]].
- **Spelling:** [[nous mangeons]], [[nous commençons]]; but [[je commence]] has no ç, because *c* before *e* is already soft.

blocks.title: Déjeuner, dîner, souper
blocks.body:
The names of meals are different in Québec and in France, and they are also -er verbs:

- **Québec:** [[le déjeuner]] (breakfast), [[le dîner]] (lunch), [[le souper]] (supper/dinner).
- **France:** [[le petit-déjeuner]] (breakfast), [[le déjeuner]] (lunch), [[le dîner]] (dinner).

So a colleague in Montréal who says [[On dîne à midi ?]] means *lunch*. In France, [[dîner]] is the evening meal. When in doubt, say the time: [[On mange à midi ?]]

examples.en: Shall we have lunch at noon? (Québec)

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Repeat each line out loud. Keep the silent endings silent.

lines.tip: travaille ends in a y sound: tra-vaï.
mangeons: the e is silent, it only changes the spelling.
commencez ends in an é sound.

blocks.fr: Ils écoutent la radio le soir.
blocks.en: They listen to the radio in the evening.
blocks.prompt: How many people listen to the radio?
blocks.explain: You hear a z sound before [[écoutent]]: [[ils‿écoutent]]. Without the z, it would be [[il écoute]].

blocks.prompt: What time do the speakers start?
blocks.explain: [[neuf heures]] = 9:00. Notice the v sound in the liaison: neu-v‿heures.

blocks.explain: [[le matin]] alone means *in the morning*; French has no -ing form, so [[je travaille]] covers it.
[[nous commençons]] takes ç before -ons. [[On commence]] is the everyday spoken version.

blocks.prompt: In the evening, I cook with my husband.
accept: Le soir, je cuisine avec mon mari.
Je cuisine avec mon mari le soir.
Je cuisine le soir avec mon mari.
blocks.explain: [[Le soir]] can start or end the sentence, with no preposition.

blocks.prompt: Match each verb to its meaning.

blocks.explain: [[rentre]] and [[rentrent]] sound the same, so both spellings are accepted.

blocks.text: Ma sœur ___ à Toronto et elle ___ l'après-midi. (habiter, travailler)
blocks.en: My sister lives in Toronto and she works in the afternoon.
blocks.explain: Habiter and travailler are both regular -er verbs: elle → -e.

blocks.prompt: How do you say “I'm listening to the radio”?
blocks.explain: One verb, no “am”, no “to”, and je → j' before a vowel.
optionFeedback: Don't add être: j'écoute already means I'm listening.
je becomes j' before a vowel.

blocks.prompt: A new colleague asks about your day. Say when you start and finish work or classes, when you get home, and one thing you do in the evening.
checklist: Je commence à… / Je termine à…

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Je travaille à Vancouver. Je commence à 9 heures et je termine à 17 heures. Je rentre à 18 heures. Le soir, je cuisine et on mange à 19 heures. À 20 heures, on regarde la télé.
models.en: I work in Vancouver. I start at 9 and I finish at 5 p.m. I get home at 6. In the evening, I cook and we eat at 7. At 8, we watch TV.

blocks.prompt: Write 4 or 5 sentences about your day: the morning, the afternoon and the evening. Use at least four different verbs from this lesson.
checklist: Use le matin, l'après-midi and le soir
Give at least two exact times with à
Use one nous form (nous mangeons, nous commençons…)

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Je m'appelle Raj. Le matin, je travaille dans une banque à Toronto. Je commence à 8 heures. L'après-midi, je termine à 16 heures et je rentre. Le soir, je prépare le repas avec ma femme. Nous mangeons à 19 heures et nous écoutons la radio.
models.en: My name is Raj. In the morning, I work in a bank in Toronto. I start at 8. In the afternoon, I finish at 4 p.m. and I go home. In the evening, I prepare the meal with my wife. We eat at 7 p.m. and we listen to the radio.

summary:
- Conjugate any regular **-er** verb in the present: [[je travaille, tu travailles, il travaille, nous travaillons, vous travaillez, ils travaillent]]
- Spell [[nous mangeons]] and [[nous commençons]] correctly
- Say when you do things with [[le matin]], [[l'après-midi]], [[le soir]] and [[à 8 heures]]
